overview: Sigma 4.11's Spider climbs walls by driving the player's motionY while horizontally collided, with four modes selected by the MODE Options: Mineplex (default), Vanilla, Jump and Cubecraft. The module fires from the pre-phase of EventUpdate whenever mc.thePlayer.isCollidedHorizontally is true and isInsideBlock() is false: getCollidedDir() ray-casts a narrow 0.29-wide AABB (offset plus/minus 0.3000001) to find which face the player is pressed against, and the modes then act on that direction. Mineplex sets motionY to the MOTION setting (default 0.2, adjustable 0.005-3) and snaps the position 0.3 blocks into the wall on the collided axis; Vanilla simply sets motionY continuously, the classic climb; Jump triggers a vanilla jump() when motionY decays below -0.230527 or the player is grounded (snapping the position to the block boundary first) and adds a 0.006-block phase shift toward the wall, plus it cancels block bounds more than one block above the feet so the jump can pass a ceiling; Cubecraft shifts the position by 0.0625 per tick toward the wall, sets motionY, and drops mc.timer.timerSpeed to 0.3 while climbing so the client-side motion advances slower than the packets imply. onDisable restores timerSpeed to 1.

sections.p: onEvent registers EventUpdate and EventBlockBounds. The pre-phase checks the collision gate (isCollidedHorizontally and not inside a block) and calls getCollidedDir(), which returns 1-4 for the +x, -x, +z, -z faces by testing a 0.29-wide, 1.9-tall AABB offset 0.3000001 in each direction against the world's colliding bounding boxes. The mode switch then applies the climb: Mineplex writes motionY and snaps the collided axis coordinate to the block boundary (em.setX((int)x - 0.3) for negative coordinates, (int)(x + 1) - 0.3 otherwise) on the +x and +z faces only; Vanilla writes motionY unconditionally; Jump conditionally jumps and nudges the position 0.006 on any face; Cubecraft nudges 0.0625 on any face, writes motionY, and sets timerSpeed 0.3. The post-gate else-branch restores timerSpeed to 1 when the Cubecraft climb ends. EventBlockBounds, in Jump mode, cancels any block box whose minY is more than one block above the player's feet, letting the jump clip a ceiling. isInsideBlock() is the same full-AABB scan shared with the Phase module and keeps the module from fighting actual embedment.

Mineplex and Vanilla are the honest climbs: a constant vertical motion (0.2 default) while the player is pressed against a wall, with the Mineplex variant aligning the player to the block face so the collision persists tick after tick - without the snap, a bumpy wall would end the collision and the climb. The MOTION setting directly controls climb speed. Jump is the burst variant: it waits until the vertical motion has decayed to -0.230527 (or the player is on the ground), snaps to the block boundary, fires a vanilla jump (motionY 0.42), and keeps the horizontal phase shift of 0.006 so the collision never lapses; the EventBlockBounds cancel removes ceiling interference. Cubecraft is the timer variant: the 0.0625 shift keeps the player glued to the wall while timerSpeed 0.3 stretches client time, so the same packet rate covers a longer server-side ascent - the server sees a normal packet cadence while the client moves slower, which is the mode's intended bypass of packet-rate checks.

files.label: Spider.java (module)
files.explanation: The module is self-contained in this file. EventUpdate pre holds the collision gate, the getCollidedDir() face detection, and the four-mode switch; EventBlockBounds carries the Jump mode's ceiling exemption; getCollidedDir() builds the 0.29-wide probe AABB and tests the four offsets; isInsideBlock() shares the Phase module's full-cube scan (including the BlockHopper special case). The only cross-module touch is onDisable resetting mc.timer.timerSpeed to 1, which the Cubecraft mode borrows and restores. There are no packet injections anywhere - the climb is expressed entirely through motionY and the position modifications EventUpdate applies to the player before the tick's movement packets are assembled, which is why the C03 stream simply shows a player ascending a wall at an unnatural constant vertical speed.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical physics envelope)
countering.explanation: SurvivalFly's vDistRel accepts exactly four vertical envelopes: a zero-y move on ground, a jump, a step-up and a riptide launch. Everything else is a violation scaled by 100 with a set-back. A spider climb presents a constant positive y-distance per tick - 0.2 blocks in the default configuration, or up to 3 with the MOTION setting maxed - while the player is horizontally collided with a wall, which matches none of the four envelopes: it is not a jump (no jump signature, and it repeats every tick for the whole climb), not a step (no ground under the wall face), and not riptide. The violation fires on the second tick of the climb and the set-back drops the player off the wall. The Jump mode's periodic jumps are envelope-shaped on the jump tick itself, but the intervening climb ticks (motionY driven to 0.065 and the 0.006 phase shifts) are not, and NCP ray-traces ground, so the mode cannot disguise the sustained ascent. The packet's onGround flag is irrelevant throughout, because NCP's ground state comes from the block cache, not the flag.

countering.label: Flight17 (vertical speed limits)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight17 check is the 1.7/1.8-compatible flight check and runs its limits from config: maxAscendSpeed, maxDescendSpeed, maxHover and the ladder-specific ladder_ascend / ladder_instant / ladder_descend paths. It reads the player's vertical speed from MovingData, and when the player is ascending it compares against maxAscendSpeed, with a separate instant-ladder patch that catches an immediate jump to climb speed, and it limits how long a player can hover in air. The ladder branch only legitimizes vertical motion while the player is actually on a ladder block.

A Spider climb is vertical motion at a constant speed (0.2 default) with no ladder block under the player and no ground contact, so it is scored as an illegitimate ascend: vertical > maxAscendSpeed flags the sustained climb, and the mineplex wall-snap means the player's position is pinned to the face while the vertical component keeps rising. The Jump mode's bursts produce alternating positive and negative vertical speeds that trip the hover timer instead, because the player never touches ground between jumps. The MOTION setting at low values (0.005) is the bypass surface - climbs slow enough to stay under maxAscendSpeed pass this check, which is why the module's default is 0.2 and the setting exists at all.

countering.label: Fly (expected vertical velocity)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Fly check computes the next expected vertical velocity from the previous one using the vanilla physics model - gravity, jump impulse, water and ladder handling - and compares the actual move's vertical delta against the expected value (with the check skipping players on climbable blocks, in water, or with accepted knockback). The ladder exemption is explicit in the check's own comment: without a fastladder check, players can 'pop' off climbables, which is precisely the kind of motion the module produces on a non-ladder wall.

The Mineplex and Vanilla climbs fail the expected-velocity model because the model predicts motionY decaying by gravity every tick (0.42, then roughly -0.08 per tick until terminal velocity), while the module writes a constant 0.2: the actual vertical delta matches no predicted step, so the discrepancy accumulates and the punishment (rubber-band) fires after the threshold. The Jump mode is the subtle case - its jump() tick is exactly the predicted impulse, so the check sees a legitimate jump, but the 0.006 phase shift on the same tick displaces the horizontal position into the wall, and the repeated jump cycle without ground contact diverges from the model's jump-from-ground requirement. The 0.2 default is far enough from the 0.42 jump impulse that the vertical mismatch is unambiguous.
